bronze plaque beside the door","title":"To whoever comes with a light","sig":"Ilvaris, who eats candles","pages":["Thief, you have brought me a light. Good. I have been so hungry.

Where my bearers kneel, the masons’ road shows only to those who dim their own.

Where my eyes sleep, keep them sleeping. Go as the blind go: by pole, and by patience.

My bells remember the order of their making. Ring them as they were cast.

My hall breathes fire. Cross it while it draws breath.","Give your flame to the hook, and let the mirrors carry it to the sun.

What I loved, I kept in humble wood.

There is a road across my gulf. Your lantern lies about it.

Three faces guard my sleep. Weep not, laugh not. Dream.

And when at last you find me, bring fire. In the dark I am only smoke."]},{"id":"stairText","type":"inscription","style":"look","wall":[[34,60],"s"],"caption":"The stair you came down","title":"Sealed","pages":["The stair-slab ground shut the moment your feet left the last step. The masons who laid this floor walked home each evening by their own marks. The marks are faint.

Bronze is bright when it is young, and greens as the long years pass.

Wake them in the order they were poured, eldest first, or wake my gardeners instead."]},{"id":"crystalText","type":"inscription","style":"look","wall":[[38,12],"n"],"caption":"Beside the north door","title":"A sun-crystal","pages":["A disc of clear crystal is set into the wall next to the door, cold and dark. The door has no handle, no keyhole, no hinge you can see."]},{"id":"journalText","type":"inscription","style":"book","pos":[85200,10800],"caption":"An open book on the lectern","title":"The journal of Ilvaris","sig":"in a small, careful hand","pages":["Year of the Last Lamp.

The city burns its oil all night, as though the night were an enemy. Fools. The night is a larder.","I have learned to drink a flame. It goes down like warm honey, and I do not grow older.

Every lamp in the lower quarter is mine now. They light them again each evening. They think it is the wind.","They came for me with torches, which was very thoughtful of them.","A weakness I must remember. My body forgets itself in the dark. In shadow I am smoke and soot; only in firelight do I recall that I have hands, and can be cut.

I shall keep my sanctum black.","They have sealed me under the hill with all my stolen lights. Let them. Someone always comes with a lantern.

What I treasure I keep in plain wood.
